concept.centerRule: Explicit sin-family wording establishes the center. Related terms such as iniquity, transgression, trespass, lawlessness, guilt, evil, and suffering enter only where a bounded source states the relation.

characterAnchors.label: Cain
characterAnchors.note: Receives the first explicit warning about sin before killing Abel.

characterAnchors.label: Moses
characterAnchors.note: Names sin, seeks atonement, asks forgiveness, and teaches accountability.

characterAnchors.label: David
characterAnchors.note: Confesses after Nathan’s charge and stands within prayers for cleansing and restored joy.

characterAnchors.label: Isaiah
characterAnchors.note: Receives cleansing in the throne vision and speaks of the servant bearing sins.

characterAnchors.label: John the Baptist
characterAnchors.note: Receives confessed sins at the Jordan and identifies Jesus as the Lamb who takes away the world’s sin.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus Christ
characterAnchors.note: Is named with saving, forgiving, remission, bearing, freedom, death, resurrection, and restored life.

characterAnchors.label: Peter
characterAnchors.note: Announces remission through Jesus’ name and later writes of Christ bearing sins.

characterAnchors.label: Paul
characterAnchors.note: Traces sin with law, death, grace, slavery, reconciliation, resurrection, and life.

characterAnchors.label: John
characterAnchors.note: Preserves difficult statements about having and practicing sin, advocacy, death, washing, and remembered judgment.

concept.throughline: The subject moves from sin crouching at Cain’s door through law, offerings, confession, consequence, forgiveness, prophetic promise, Jesus’ relation to sins, apostolic arguments about law and death, and final visions of cleansing and judgment.
